articles.headline: Donald Trump wins US Presidential election to become 47th President
articles.summary: Donald Trump has won the US Presidential election, defeating Kamala Harris. He secured over 270 electoral votes, marking a historic return to the White House. World leaders have congratulated Trump on his victory. The win is expected to influence global trade, immigration policies, and international relations significantly over the next four years.

articles.headline: Cabinet approves PM-Vidyalaxmi scheme for financial support to students
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet has approved the PM-Vidyalaxmi scheme to provide financial assistance to meritorious students for higher education. The scheme offers collateral-free, guarantor-free loans up to Rs 10 lakh for students in top-quality higher educational institutions. It aims to ensure that financial constraints do not hinder talented students from pursuing professional education.

articles.headline: Sensex drops 900 points as US election results trigger volatility
articles.summary: Indian equity markets witnessed a sharp decline with the Sensex falling over 900 points and Nifty slipping below 24,300. The crash was triggered by global market volatility following Donald Trump's victory in the US elections. Major losers included tech and pharma stocks, while the US dollar strengthened against the rupee, impacting emerging market sentiment.

articles.headline: Tata Motors Q2 net profit falls 11% to Rs 3,764 crore
articles.summary: Tata Motors reported an 11% year-on-year decline in its consolidated net profit to Rs 3,764 crore for the second quarter ended September 2024. The fall was attributed to sluggish demand in the domestic commercial vehicle segment and higher marketing costs. However, Jaguar Land Rover maintained a steady performance despite global supply chain challenges.

articles.headline: Government to sell 2.5% stake in Mazagon Dock via OFS
articles.summary: The Indian government has announced plans to sell a 2.5% stake in Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders through an Offer for Sale (OFS). The floor price has been set at a discount to the current market price. The move is part of the government's disinvestment target for the current fiscal year to raise capital for various infrastructure and social welfare projects.

articles.headline: Apollo Hospitals Q2 net profit surges 63% on higher occupancy
articles.summary: Apollo Hospitals Enterprise reported a 63% jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 379 crore for the September quarter. Revenue growth was driven by improved healthcare services and higher digital health platform volumes. The company saw increased occupancy rates across its hospital network and significant expansion in its pharmacy distribution business.

articles.headline: GST Council likely to reduce tax on insurance premiums soon
articles.summary: The GST Council is expected to discuss a proposal to reduce or waive the 18% GST on life and health insurance premiums in its upcoming meeting. A group of ministers has been reviewing the tax structure to make insurance more affordable. The move could provide relief to millions of policyholders and boost insurance penetration across the country.

articles.headline: Germany's ruling coalition collapses as Scholz fires Finance Minister
articles.summary: Germany's three-party ruling coalition has collapsed after Chancellor Olaf Scholz fired Finance Minister Christian Lindner. The move followed months of disputes over economic policy and budget spending. Scholz announced plans for a vote of confidence in January, which could lead to early elections in March, adding to political uncertainty in the Eurozone.

articles.headline: India set to face South Africa in four-match T20 series
articles.summary: The Indian cricket team is scheduled to play a four-match T20 International series against South Africa starting this week. The series will feature a young Indian squad led by Suryakumar Yadav. Key players are looking to solidify their spots ahead of the upcoming international calendar. South Africa has named a full-strength squad for the home series.

articles.headline: IT industry braces for H-1B visa changes under Trump administration
articles.summary: The Indian IT services sector is preparing for potential changes to the H-1B visa program following Donald Trump's election victory. Experts suggest that stricter immigration rules and increased scrutiny on work visas could lead to higher costs for Indian tech firms. Companies may increase local hiring in the US to mitigate risks associated with policy shifts.

articles.headline: Walmart International CEO Chris Nicholas Expected to Visit India Next Week
articles.summary: Walmart’s international business chief Chris Nicholas is slated to visit India on Monday to meet Flipkart leadership. The visit follows the announced departure of Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy, effective December 4. Nicholas is expected to address employee concerns regarding stock options (Esops) and leadership transitions as the e-commerce giant navigates potential IPO delays.

articles.headline: Nitin Gadkari and Top Policymakers to Chart India’s 2047 Development Roadmap
articles.summary: The Economic Times is set to host the second edition of the 'India Ascends' summit on December 1. Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and Shaktikanta Das, principal secretary to the PM, will lead discussions on scaling infrastructure, technology, and exports. The event focuses on achieving the 'Viksit Bharat 2047' vision through self-reliance and global competitiveness.

articles.headline: Centre Plans Minimum Quality Standards for Cybersecurity Tools on GeM Portal
articles.summary: The government is developing benchmarks for cybersecurity products sold to state bodies and PSUs via the Government e-Marketplace (GeM). The move aims to address performance failures and emerging AI threats. Standards will cover software, network equipment, and forensic tools, requiring OEMs to provide certification and undergo verification by agencies like CERT-In and STQC.

articles.headline: HDFC Bank Insources Digital Platforms to Mitigate Rising Third-Party Cyber Risks
articles.summary: HDFC Bank is bringing critical digital banking and payment platforms in-house following a surge in cyberattacks on third-party fintech vendors. The bank aims to maintain 70% of its key applications internally, including mobile and net banking. This strategy follows a recent wave of payment API attacks affecting 20 financial institutions and causing losses of over Rs 300 crore.

articles.headline: IBM Orders US Employees on H-1B Visas to Relocate Abroad
articles.summary: Technology major IBM has given some US-based employees on H-1B visas and green cards three weeks to relocate overseas or leave the company. The decision primarily affects the consulting division as the firm ends most immigration sponsorships. Impacted workers were offered three months of severance if they decline transfers, with many roles expected to shift to India.

articles.headline: Global Trading Partners Protest New Round of Trump Administration Tariffs
articles.summary: Major economies including China, the EU, Brazil, and Singapore expressed disappointment and signaled potential retaliation after the US announced new tariffs. The Trump administration aims to impose levies to combat excess manufacturing capacity. While Singapore urged reconsideration of 20% duties, Brazil vowed not to yield, and China labeled the move as political maneuvering.

articles.headline: S&P Global Places Nvidia Credit Rating on Downgrade Watch
articles.summary: S&P Global Ratings has warned of a possible downgrade for Nvidia, citing weaknesses in management and board independence following the temporary departure and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang. The agency noted that corporate governance has not kept pace with the firm's rapid growth. Nvidia's five-year credit default swap (CDS) spreads jumped sharply in response to the leadership turmoil.

articles.headline: FIFA Reports Cyberattack Resulting in Limited Personal Data Breach
articles.summary: Soccer’s world governing body, FIFA, confirmed it was the victim of a cyberattack that compromised a limited set of personal and business information. The Handsome Boy Hacking Club reportedly claimed credit for leaking over 12 gigabytes of internal documents. FIFA stated it is working with law enforcement and condemned the unlawful acquisition of data as a violation of privacy.

articles.headline: HMSI Shifts Focus to Dealer Margins Over Two-Wheeler Market Share
articles.summary: Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India (HMSI) president Tsutsumu Otani stated the company will prioritize dealer profitability and customer retention over annual volume rankings. The firm is targeting the 'units in operation' metric rather than chasing market leadership. HMSI expects festive sales to exceed 1.9 million units and plans to increase its focus on the premium motorcycle segment.

articles.headline: Nearly 65% of New GCC Fresher Jobs Require Specialized AI Skills
articles.summary: A report by Adecco India reveals that 65% of new entry-level roles in Global Capability Centres (GCCs) now demand AI capabilities. AI-related demand for freshers grew 45% in 2026, significantly outperforming routine IT services hiring. Companies are increasingly recruiting graduates for technology roles and providing in-house training in data engineering and data science.

articles.headline: Sebi to Investigate Governance Concerns in Tata Steel-APL Apollo Deal
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India will seek details on a multipronged deal where Tata Steel plans to acquire a controlling stake in APL Apollo Tubes for Rs 28,000 crore. Institutional investors and proxy firms like SES have raised concerns that the structure favors outgoing promoters over minority shareholders. APL Apollo shares have dropped 30% since the announcement.

articles.headline: Climate Finance is Responsibility Not Generosity, Says Minister Bhupender Yadav
articles.summary: Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav told ET that developed countries are obliged to provide financial resources for climate assistance to developing nations. Following the deadlock at COP 31, Yadav emphasized that success should be measured by tangible results and improved lives rather than new declarations. He called for a focus on affordable technology access and adaptation.

articles.headline: Priyanka Gandhi Seeks MEA Intervention to Trace Missing Indians in SE Asia
articles.summary: Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra has written to External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar regarding 20 Keralam residents reported missing in Vietnam, Thailand, and Cambodia. The individuals, primarily from Wayanad, had stopped contacting their families after taking up jobs in those countries. Vadra urged the ministry to investigate their whereabouts and ensure their safety.

articles.headline: Wayanad Set to Become India’s First Electronic Waste-Free District
articles.summary: Wayanad is poised to be declared India's first e-waste-free district after a campaign collected 102.85 metric tonnes of electronic waste from households. Led by Minister T Siddique with support from MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, the initiative involved scientific disposal through authorized recyclers. The project is part of a broader goal to make the district climate-positive.

articles.headline: Sumitomo Corporation Proposes 100-Acre Japanese Industrial Park Near Bengaluru
articles.summary: Japan's Sumitomo Corporation has expressed interest in developing a private industrial park to attract Japanese manufacturers to Karnataka. Large and Medium Industries Minister MB Patil discussed the proposal during his Japan visit. The talks also covered Mukand Sumi Special Steel's planned Rs 2,000 crore investment in Koppal and potential expansions by Meiji Seika Pharma.

articles.headline: RBI Shifts 84% of Total Gold Holdings to Domestic Vaults
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India increased its share of gold held domestically to 84% (740.13 tonnes) by September 2026, up from 65.4% a year earlier. While total holdings remained steady at 880.52 tonnes, the central bank reduced its storage with the Bank of England and the Bank for International Settlements. Gold now accounts for 14.38% of India's total foreign exchange reserves.

articles.headline: Dubai Islamic Bank to Acquire Emirates Islamic in 8.5 Billion Dollar Deal
articles.summary: Dubai Islamic Bank (DIB) has announced an all-stock acquisition of Emirates Islamic Bank, creating a global Islamic banking giant with $159 billion in assets. DIB will issue 3.49 billion new shares to Emirates NBD, which will hold a 32.5% stake in the merged entity. The deal aims to combine DIB's corporate strength with Emirates Islamic's retail deposit base.

articles.headline: Banks to Ease Credit Norms for PM Surya Ghar Rooftop Solar Loans
articles.summary: Lenders are set to relax credit score requirements for the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana to boost adoption. Banks will move beyond rigid 650+ credit scores to assess default history and repayment records for first-time borrowers. The government aims to cover 7.5 million households by 2026, with installations currently occurring at a rate of 100,000 every six days.

articles.headline: Kaynes Semicon and Vishay Intertechnology Form Joint Venture for OSAT Expansion
articles.summary: Kaynes Semicon is partnering with US-based Vishay Intertechnology to expand its semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) capacity fourfold to 9 billion devices annually. Vishay will invest $56.4 million for a 49% stake in the venture. The partnership includes a captive production line for Vishay and plans to manufacture passive components like resistors and capacitors.

articles.headline: French Senate Passes Law Fining Rioters 10,000 Euros for Property Damage
articles.summary: Following violent protests causing over 1 billion euros in damage, the French Senate passed a measure allowing the state to fine participants 10,000 euros. The law holds parents liable for damages caused by minors, with fines potentially deducted from family social security allowances. The move aims to secure restitution for the destruction of public and private property.

articles.headline: Engineering and B-school graduates face hiring uncertainty for class of 2027
articles.summary: Companies are reworking campus hiring plans, favoring experienced talent over freshers due to global uncertainty and AI disruption. Placement teams at IITs and IIMs are expanding recruiter lists as recruitment for fewer positions becomes a concern. High-frequency trading firms are offering higher packages but for niche specialist roles rather than conventional coding positions.

articles.headline: Trump proposes fresh tariffs on Indian imports amid trade deal talks
articles.summary: The US administration has proposed new tariffs on trade partners, with Indian imports potentially facing a 25% rate. The US trade representative suggested this could drop to 17% if a long-pending bilateral trade deal is signed. India and the US had previously discussed an 18% tariff rate. Experts urge India to continue diversifying trade partners while negotiating with Washington.

articles.headline: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO closes with 1.52 times overall subscription
articles.summary: The ₹8,981-crore IPO of Mahanadi Coalfields closed with a subscription of 1.52 times, primarily driven by institutional buyers. Qualified institutional portion was taken nearly five times, while retail investors subscribed to just 0.46 times their portion. The IPO comprised a 10% stake sale by parent company Coal India. Mahanadi was India’s top coal producer in FY26.

articles.headline: US economy grows 4.3% in September quarter despite persistent inflation
articles.summary: The US economy grew at a 4.3% annual rate in the September quarter, its fastest pace in three years. Growth exceeded previous estimates despite the Federal Reserve's efforts to curb inflation. The personal consumption expenditures price index rose to 3.8% in October, complicating the outlook for future interest rate cuts as markets price in a possible December hike.

articles.headline: Indian vehicle retail sales growth slows sharply during festive season
articles.summary: Vehicle retail bookings grew just 2.2% this festive season, compared to 21.3% in 2025. Passenger vehicle bookings fell 7.2%, while two-wheeler growth eased to 3.7%. Analysts attribute the slowdown to a high statistical base from previous years, persistent inflation, and a hazy geopolitical outlook impacting consumer spending power across major categories.

articles.headline: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hits fastest List A double century off 52 balls
articles.summary: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set a new record in men's List A cricket by scoring 204 off 53 balls for India A against the UAE. His double century came in just 52 balls, breaking the previous record of 103 balls. The innings included 28 sixes, the most in any men’s List A innings. List A includes one-day internationals and domestic 50-over games.

articles.headline: Tata Sons plans public listing within six months following board proposal
articles.summary: Tata Sons has added an IPO plan to its board agenda for 30 November, targeting a six-month timeline for listing after shareholder approval. The proposal includes hiring bankers and advisers for the public offering. The move comes amid internal tensions with Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata, who has previously expressed opposition to the listing of the group's holding company.

articles.headline: Sebi proposes twelve year lifetime cap on market institution MD tenures
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has proposed a 12-year lifetime cap for managing directors across market infrastructure institutions. The move could potentially end Ashishkumar Chauhan’s tenure at the National Stock Exchange in July 2027. Chauhan would be ineligible for another term having already spent a decade at BSE before joining the NSE.

articles.headline: Severe El Niño creates food and water crisis risks in India
articles.summary: A deficient monsoon driven by El Niño has impacted crops across six Indian states, leading to rising food prices and low reservoir levels. Winter sowing is currently lagging, and the fallout is expected to stretch into 2027. The environmental conditions are putting pressure on the wider economy as farmers struggle with supply shortages and reduced water availability.

articles.headline: Haleon in early talks to acquire controlling stake in HealthKart
articles.summary: UK-based consumer health firm Haleon is in early discussions to acquire a controlling stake in HealthKart, an Indian nutrition and supplements startup. The deal could value HealthKart at $1.2-1.4 billion. Haleon, a spinoff from GSK, is looking to diversify its portfolio in India beyond traditional brands like Eno and Sensodyne. HealthKart is alternately exploring an Indian listing.

articles.headline: Memory chip shortage to cause first annual smartphone revenue decline
articles.summary: India's smartphone market faces its first revenue decline in 2026 due to a global memory chip shortage that is driving up handset prices. Unit sales are expected to fall by at least 20% this year. The shortage is hitting both volume and affordability, with brands like Samsung, Vivo, and Xiaomi expected to feel the pinch as production costs rise due to AI-driven component demand.

articles.headline: Airtel and Jio resist Trai order to display base plans upfront
articles.summary: Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel are pushing back against a Trai directive to prominently display cheaper mandated tariff plans on their apps and websites. The telcos are concerned that high visibility for lower-priced packs, including voice-only and calendar month plans, could hurt average revenue per user. Trai noted consumers currently face difficulty finding these low-cost options.

articles.headline: Lenders recover 31% of admitted claims from large stressed companies
articles.summary: Data from the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India shows creditors recovered 31.1% of admitted claims from 218 large stressed firms with defaults over ₹1,000 crore. This recovery rate is slightly higher than the 30.2% average across all IBC cases. Experts note that larger assets often attract stronger investor interest, though prolonged delays remain a major hurdle for value recovery.

articles.headline: GST registration cancellations to become automatic starting 1 December
articles.summary: The finance ministry has amended GST rules to allow automatic processing of registration cancellations for taxpayers who have filed all returns and cleared liabilities. The move aims to reduce administrative intervention and procedural delays. Previously, tax officers were required to review routine applications within 30 days, a process that often faced significant delays.

articles.headline: Centre considers easing local content rules to attract global shipbuilders
articles.summary: India is looking to lower domestic content requirements under the Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme to lure major global players like Samsung Heavy Industries. Currently, shipbuilders must meet a 40% local content mandate for full incentives. Coastal states like Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh are offering additional subsidies to make India a competitive shipbuilding destination.

articles.headline: Youth urge Budget 2027-28 to prioritize job creation and technology
articles.summary: During the final pre-budget consultation, young people called for the Union Budget 2027-28 to focus on job creation, industry-relevant skills, and emerging technologies. The demands highlighted the need for a framework that aligns education with the needs of a modern digital economy and provides support for domestic manufacturing to boost employment opportunities.

articles.headline: Road ministry proposes tighter eligibility rules for highway contractors
articles.summary: The road ministry has proposed new rules linking the bidding capacity of highway contractors to their past execution records and performance ratings. The framework aims to curb project delays and strengthen accountability. The changes would update the 2019 model request for proposal for projects awarded under the engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) mode.

articles.headline: India Post leverages modernization fund to reach profitability by 2030
articles.summary: Union minister Jyotiraditya Scindia stated that India Post aims to turn profitable by 2030 by leveraging a ₹2,632-crore cabinet-approved fund for modernization. The department will focus on new product launches and improved operational efficiency. The schemes are designed to strengthen postal infrastructure and services across the country to compete in the logistics market.

articles.headline: Gold prices rebound to 1.27 lakh as rupee declines further
articles.summary: Gold prices in the national capital rose by ₹1,500 to ₹1.27 lakh per 10 grams on Thursday. The recovery was supported by a falling rupee and renewed buying interest at lower price levels. Precious metals had recently seen volatility due to global economic shifts and changing expectations regarding US interest rate moves.

articles.headline: Finnable raises 405 crore in Series C funding for technology
articles.summary: Digital lender Finnable has raised ₹405 crore in a Series C round to strengthen its proprietary technology and expand lending partnerships. Investors included Bharat Value Fund, Pratithi Investments, and NKSquared. The Bengaluru-based non-banking financial company plans to use the capital to fuel business growth and expand its reach in the consumer credit market.

articles.headline: Data centre operators increase borrowings to fuel artificial intelligence race
articles.summary: Combined borrowings of six major data centre firms in India rose 43% to ₹27,062 crore in FY26 as they expand capacity for AI. AdaniConneX, Nxtra, and Yotta are among firms leading the debt-funded expansion. India's data centre capacity is projected to triple by 2030, but standalone firms are currently taking on debt faster than their revenues are growing to capture market share.

articles.headline: Kalyan Silks explores minority stake sale at 3,000 crore valuation
articles.summary: Promoters of Kerala-based textile retailer Kalyan Silks are seeking a minority stake sale that could value the firm at up to ₹3,000 crore. The 20% stake sale may include primary and secondary components as the firm prepares for a potential public listing. The company reported a net profit of ₹113.55 crore in FY25 and operates across India and the Middle East.

articles.headline: GEF Capital Partners to invest 615 million in climate technology
articles.summary: Private equity firm GEF Capital Partners has raised $615 million for its fourth India-focused fund. The firm plans to back more than a dozen companies in energy transition, industrial decarbonization, and circular economy sectors. GEF is particularly bullish on the cooling value chain, identifying increased energy demand for cooling driven by AI and data centres.

articles.headline: Hedgeye analysts offer conflicting views on newly listed Anthropic stock
articles.summary: Two analysts at Hedgeye Risk Management have published opposing views on Anthropic PBC. While one analyst believes the stock is attractive for long-term investors following its IPO, another has recommended a short position due to concerns over data centre financing and long-term business demand. The split reflects broader market uncertainty over valuing disruptive AI potential.

articles.headline: Max Healthcare shares recover 30% as hospital capacity utilisation improves
articles.summary: Max Healthcare shares have gained 30% in a month as investors reassess earnings risks following regulatory caps on anti-cancer drug margins. The recovery is supported by steady 77% occupancy and plans to add 1,400 beds next year. Analysts have upgraded the stock despite seasonal weakness, citing strong revenue growth from international patients and institutional mix improvements.

articles.headline: Indian banks raise deposit rates as liquidity cushion from FCNR fades
articles.summary: Lenders including HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank are raising rates on select term deposits as system liquidity tightens. The temporary boost from foreign currency non-resident (bank) inflows has tapered, and credit growth continues to outpace deposit accretion. Smaller finance banks are offering up to 8.6%, while larger banks are targeting specific tenures to attract sticky funding.

articles.headline: NSE market capitalization nears 6 trillion as shares hit record high
articles.summary: Shares of the National Stock Exchange of India hit a record high of ₹2,400 on Thursday, bringing its market capitalization close to ₹6 trillion. The exchange is now ranked ninth in domestic market cap rankings. The stock has surged over 29% since its debut on the BSE in September, supported by strong financial performance and growing trading volumes in the Indian market.

articles.headline: Equity placements through QIPs and preferential issues surge in FY27
articles.summary: Listed firms raised ₹1.61 trillion through preferential issues and ₹85,502 crore via QIPs in the first eight months of the fiscal year, exceeding all of FY26. Mutual funds accounted for nearly 60% of QIP allocations. Promoters emerged as the biggest drivers of preferential fundraising, committing their own capital to support growth plans amid a rising interest rate environment.

articles.headline: Adani Enterprises and Adani Power plan 2,000 crore bond sale
articles.summary: Two Adani Group firms are looking to raise at least ₹2,000 crore through public bond offerings to diversify funding sources. Adani Enterprises and Adani Power are working with local arrangers for sales targeted by March. The move would boost India's public debt market, which is currently dominated by private placements, and help the conglomerate broaden its domestic investor base.

articles.headline: GE Shipping halts fleet expansion due to surging second-hand vessel prices
articles.summary: Great Eastern Shipping Co. has put fleet expansion on hold as wars in West Asia and Ukraine drive up vessel prices. The company is instead using its ₹8,500 crore cash pile for share buybacks, viewing them as a cheaper way to gain exposure to its fleet. Prices for five-year-old Suezmax vessels have surged 58% in six months, making new acquisitions less attractive.

articles.headline: Sebi appoints forensic auditor for Mysore Amalgamated Coffee Estates probe
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has appointed Indus Value Consulting as a forensic auditor to investigate Coffee Day Enterprises. The probe follows a tribunal directive to examine the alleged diversion of ₹3,535 crore from subsidiaries to an entity linked to the promoters. The investigation aims to resolve long-standing allegations of securities law violations.

articles.headline: Nvidia executive relationship with Super Micro officer raises conflict concerns
articles.summary: Nvidia's former sales head Jay Puri married an executive from Super Micro Computer while the firms were competing for chip access. Super Micro is currently facing a Justice Department investigation into allegations of chip smuggling to China. While the couple denies professional gain from the relationship, it has raised concerns regarding conflicts of interest in the AI chip supply chain.

articles.headline: Wild market swings and AI demand pose dilemma for Fed chairman
articles.summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh faces a choice between raising rates to curb sticky inflation or pausing due to recent tech stock volatility. Some officials worry AI is fueling demand that could keep price pressures high. However, sustained market declines could act as a form of tightening, potentially reducing the need for more rate hikes if economic activity slows naturally.

articles.headline: US officials split over espionage claims involving Nvidia chief's affair
articles.summary: Senior US national security officials are debating whether Alice Huang, who had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, was passing information to Chinese intelligence. While the FBI and CIA have collected reports on her contacts, there is no consensus on whether she was an active asset. The debate follows President Trump's recent push to reinstate Huang as CEO.

articles.headline: OPEC plus alliance considers rolling over oil output quotas to January
articles.summary: Delegates indicate that OPEC+ is considering maintaining current oil output quotas through January due to market uncertainties linked to the Iran war. The alliance, led by Saudi Arabia, faces internal strains as some members push for higher production limits. A meeting on Sunday will determine targets for 2027 amid fluctuating global demand and geopolitical tensions.

articles.headline: Parliament special sitting from 30 November to continue Monsoon Session
articles.summary: The Centre has sought to reconvene Parliament for a three-day special sitting starting 30 November. The sitting is technically a continuation of the Monsoon Session, which was never formally prorogued. The move has led to speculation regarding potential legislation for women's reservation and delimitation, though the specific government business agenda has not been fully disclosed.

articles.headline: Congress party sues Meta over alleged restriction of Gandhi's posts
articles.summary: The Indian National Congress has sued Meta in the Delhi High Court, alleging the platform arbitrarily restricted posts featuring leader Rahul Gandhi. The party argues that India's social media rules are being misused to block lawful political content. The petition seeks the restoration of restricted posts and greater transparency regarding the automated censorship systems used by Meta.

articles.headline: Health ministry tightens controls on experimental autism stem cell treatments
articles.summary: The Union health ministry has barred clinics from offering stem cell treatment for autism as routine care, mandating that it only be provided through approved clinical trials. New regulations require institutions to insure participants against research-related harm and prohibit charging for experimental treatment. The ministry stressed that autism has no cure and requires therapy over drugs.

articles.headline: India draws 31 billion in climate funding but mostly for transport
articles.summary: India has attracted $31 billion in climate and sustainability equity funding since 2021, according to a report by BCG and IVCA. However, over 90% of the funds have flowed into power, low-carbon fuels, and transport. Sectors like manufacturing, waste management, and agriculture remain underfunded. India requires estimated annual investments of $500 billion to reach its 2070 climate goals.

articles.headline: Global memory chip shortage sends prices of consumer electronics soaring
articles.summary: A massive supply crunch in memory chips has forced global electronics manufacturers to raise prices by up to 10 times for specific components. The AI boom has redirected supply to data centers, leaving makers of laptops, gaming consoles, and appliances scrambling for stock. Some firms have resorted to the gray market or eBay to find units, with the shortage expected to last until 2028.

articles.headline: Pet insurance gains traction in India as veterinary costs continue rising
articles.summary: India's pet insurance market has grown 65% since 2023, though adoption remains below 1%. Most base policies cover major hospitalizations and surgeries but exclude routine outpatient care (OPD), which forms the bulk of pet expenses. Fragmentation in the veterinary sector and lack of standardized billing remain hurdles, leading many pet parents to rely on separate emergency funds.

articles.headline: New income tax law focuses on rewriting code but misses process
articles.summary: While the Income Tax Act 2025 has rewritten the law, experts argue it fails to address the underlying administrative processes that lead to millions of unresolved demands. A second Business Process Re-engineering is urged to simplify filing-to-closure chains. Millions of petty direct tax demands dating back decades continue to hold up refunds and generate litigation for taxpayers.

articles.headline: India prioritizes development of reusable rockets to slash space launch costs
articles.summary: Following SpaceX's recent milestones, India is accelerating its Reusable Launch Vehicle (RLV) program, Pushpak. The winged vehicle is designed to land horizontally like the Space Shuttle. Mastering re-entry technology and multiple ignition cycles is critical for the commercial space market. Collaboration between Isro and private firms is seen as essential to compete in global satellite launches.

articles.headline: RBI monetary policy benefits from fortuitous alignment of growth and inflation
articles.summary: Governor Sanjay Malhotra's shift to a tighter monetary policy stance in October was supported by a simultaneous surge in domestic inflation and global capital flight. Robust GDP growth above 7% allowed for higher rates without hurting economic activity. However, strategic vulnerabilities remain, particularly India's high dependence on China for critical electronic component imports.

articles.headline: Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in Parliament next week
articles.summary: The Union government has called a special sitting of Parliament starting Monday to likely table an amended Delimitation Bill. The Bill proposes a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats and a 25-year extension on using the 1971 Census to determine state proportional strength. The move comes after both Houses were adjourned without prorogation for 105 days.

articles.headline: Supreme Court agrees to list plea on Karthigai Deepam lighting row
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will hear a petition alleging the Tamil Nadu government failed to light the Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar on Thirupparankundram Hill. The plea seeks a personal affidavit from the Chief Secretary regarding the decision-making process and any role played by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. The court had previously ordered the ceremonial lighting.

articles.headline: NCLAT clears ₹480 crore for Jet Airways staff dues
articles.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal approved the release of ₹480 crore to settle gratuity and provident fund dues for Jet Airways employees. The tribunal set a two-week deadline for payments. It rejected appeals from financial creditors including SBI. Gratuity will be paid to bank accounts, while PF contributions will be deposited via the PF office.

articles.headline: Amit Shah accuses Congress of obstructing 33% women’s quota
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah asserted that the Congress cannot stop the implementation of the 33% reservation for women lawmakers in Parliament and State Assemblies. He accused the opposition of historical obstruction and reiterated the BJP's commitment to implementing the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in party-governed states.

articles.headline: Kejriwal urges Punjab women to ensure male family members vote AAP
articles.summary: Ahead of the Punjab Assembly polls, AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal urged women voters to persuade men in their families to vote for the party. Speaking at a rally in Moga, he highlighted the success of the ₹1,000 monthly financial assistance for women. He commended CM Bhagwant Mann for fulfilling party guarantees despite the state's financial challenges.

articles.headline: Jharkhand Assembly passes resolution seeking rollback of amended MMDR Act
articles.summary: The Jharkhand Legislative Assembly passed a resolution seeking the withdrawal of the amended Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act. Chief Minister Hemant Soren claimed the amendments curtail state powers to levy cess on mineral-bearing land, potentially costing the state ₹13,000 crore in annual revenue and affecting tribal welfare schemes.

articles.headline: Delhi Congress protests electoral roll irregularities on Constitution Day
articles.summary: The Delhi Congress unit organized a 'Samvidhan Raksha March' to protest alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll. General secretary K.C. Venugopal accused the government of using the Election Commission to destroy democratic values by targeting the voting rights of youth, women, and marginalized communities.

articles.headline: Women march in Delhi to end child marriage by 2030
articles.summary: Survivors of child marriage and hundreds of women participated in a candlelight march in south Delhi's Kusumpur Pahari. Led by Union Minister Savitri Thakur, the event aimed to promote the goal of eradicating child marriage in India by 2030. National Family Health Survey data shows child marriage rates in Delhi-NCR rose from 9.9% to 11.4% recently.

articles.headline: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta claims 60% of Yamuna stretch cleaned
articles.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced that 60% of the Yamuna's stretch in the capital has been cleaned. Speaking at the Brahmasthanam Mahotsav, she also launched the Amrita SREE Self-Help Group Programme to empower women through 15,000 groups across 21 states, aiming to create livelihood opportunities and promote self-reliance.

articles.headline: Court frames charges in Swaroop Nagar minor rape and murder
articles.summary: A POCSO court in Rohini framed charges against a 22-year-old man and three juveniles for the kidnapping, gang rape, and murder of a 16-year-old girl. The accused, Shivam, faces charges under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the POCSO Act. The incident occurred on September 11 in North Delhi's Swaroop Nagar.

articles.headline: Delhi Police book comedian for remarks on Bihar women and Chhath
articles.summary: Stand-up comedian Yash Maheshwari was booked by Delhi Police for making derogatory remarks against Bihari women and the Chhath festival during a show in Saket. He faces charges under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for promoting enmity and insulting the modesty of women. Maheshwari has issued an apology following similar FIRs in Patna.

articles.headline: Northern Railway denies SP MP’s claim over Saryu Kamala Express
articles.summary: Northern Railway dismissed allegations by Faizabad MP Awadhesh Prasad that he was not invited to the flag-off of the Saryu Kamala Express. Officials stated an invitation was sent to his official email on November 21. The train, connecting Ayodhya and Janakpur Dham, was virtually flagged off by the Prime Ministers of India and Nepal.

articles.headline: Delhi HC upholds charges against Lalu Prasad in IRCTC case
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court upheld the framing of charges against RJD leader Lalu Prasad, Rabri Devi, Tejashwi Yadav, and others in the IRCTC hotels case. The court found sufficient grounds to proceed with trial regarding alleged irregularities in awarding contracts to a private firm. The BJP claimed the order exposes the RJD's claims of political conspiracy.

articles.headline: Supreme Court quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan
articles.summary: The Supreme Court set aside the Bihar government's notification that allowed the premature release of former MP Anand Mohan, who was serving a life term for the 1994 murder of DM G. Krishnaiah. The court called the policy change arbitrary and directed Mohan to surrender within a month. Any future remission must involve a hearing for the victim's family.

articles.headline: Cooch Behar infant gets birth certificate after SIR-related residence row
articles.summary: District administration in Cooch Behar issued a residence certificate to the mother of a two-month-old infant who was denied a birth certificate. The delay occurred because the father's name was deleted from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision. The BDO intervention followed reports that the local BJP MLA had refused verification.

articles.headline: Rajput strongmen consolidate under Hindutva banner at Kunda katha
articles.summary: A Ram Katha hosted by Raja Bhaiya in Kunda became a venue for Rajput political mobilization. Leaders across party lines, including Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, signaled Thakur unity under the umbrella of Hindutva. Observers view the alignment as a strategic move to support CM Yogi Adityanath while maintaining caste influence ahead of upcoming elections.

articles.headline: SIT gives clean bill to ex-Minister Nagendra in Valmiki scam
articles.summary: Karnataka's Special Investigation Team found no evidence linking former Minister B. Nagendra to the ₹89.62 crore misappropriation from the Maharshi Valmiki Development Corporation. Nagendra and former chairman Basavaraj Daddal have been named as witnesses instead of accused. This contradicts findings by the CBI and ED, which implicate Nagendra as a prime suspect.

articles.headline: Congress wins deputy chairperson posts in 25 Rajasthan districts
articles.summary: The Congress party won 'up zila pramukh' positions in 25 of 37 Rajasthan districts, continuing its strong performance in Panchayati Raj elections. The ruling BJP secured positions in eight districts. Former CM Ashok Gehlot stated the results reflect public resentment against the BJP government's decision to appoint inexperienced leaders as Chief Ministers.

articles.headline: Sporadic violence marks local body polling in Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Elections for urban and gram panchayats in Andhra Pradesh concluded with incidents of violence reported in the Rayalaseema region. Clashes between NDA and YSRCP cadres occurred over alleged irregularities. Polling was held for four municipal corporations, 19 municipalities, and over 3,000 gram panchayats.

articles.headline: Court summons Union Minister's son in 2026 POCSO case
articles.summary: A POCSO court in Medchal issued summons to Bandi Bageerath, son of Union Minister Bandi Sanjay Kumar, for a case involving the alleged sexual assault and abuse of a minor girl in May 2026. Bageerath has been directed to appear before the court on January 28, 2027. He was previously arrested by Cyberabad Police after his anticipatory bail was rejected.

articles.headline: CPI(M) leader T.I. Madhusoodanan criticized for threatening social media critics
articles.summary: Former Kerala MLA T.I. Madhusoodanan faces backlash for remarks suggesting that those who insult the CPI(M) on social media would face consequences. The speech followed a court conviction of BJP workers for the murder of a party activist. A complaint has been lodged alleging incitement to violence and intimidation of the judiciary.

articles.headline: Karnataka electoral rolls reveal 17,000 cases of parent-child age anomalies
articles.summary: Analysis of Karnataka's final electoral rolls found over 17,000 entries where parent-child age gaps are less than 15 years or impossible, such as children being older than parents. Raichur and Kalaburagi recorded the highest discrepancies. Officials attribute these errors to dates of birth in documents like Aadhaar, which were flagged during the Special Intensive Revision.

articles.headline: The Siang Upper Multipurpose Project: Strategic buffer and ecological risk
articles.summary: The proposed 11,200 MW Siang dam in Arunachal Pradesh serves as a strategic counter to China's Medog project but faces resistance from indigenous tribes. Critics warn the 300-meter dam could submerge 27 villages, displace 1.5 lakh people, and starve the Assam plains of nutrient-rich silt. The project is located in a high-risk seismic zone, posing structural and flood risks.

articles.headline: Policy analysis of cash-transfer schemes and their fiscal impact
articles.summary: A report on state finances highlights that 12 Indian states will spend ₹1.68 trillion on cash-transfer schemes for women in 2025-26. Analysts argue that such social policies lack the rigour of infrastructure projects, often implemented without prior needs assessment or fiscal sustainability studies. There is a call for published social Detailed Project Reports (DPR) for scrutiny.

articles.headline: Supreme Court to test special privilege for journalists at protest sites
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will examine whether law enforcement should grant journalists special privileges at protest sites. The bench noted the need to balance journalistic freedom with public order. The case follows allegations of police abuse against media professionals during protests against the Chief Election Commissioner in October.

articles.headline: Centre informs High Court of LOC against CJP’s Saurav Das
articles.summary: The Union government informed the Delhi High Court that a Look Out Circular (LOC) was issued against Cockroach Janata Party co-convener Saurav Das by Mumbai Police. Das challenged the move after being stopped from traveling to London. The Centre claims an inquiry is verifying his passport details, while Das allege targeted harassment and privacy violations.

articles.headline: Kharge accuses BJP and RSS of being anti-Constitution
articles.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused the BJP and RSS of working to weaken the Constitution over the past 12 years. Speaking in Lucknow, he alleged that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is being used to manipulate elections by deleting names of Dalits, women, and the poor. He called for the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner.

articles.headline: Speaker Om Birla calls Constitution the foundation of democratic ethos
articles.summary: Addressing youth on Constitution Day, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla described the document as the bedrock of India's national unity and democratic identity. He highlighted the consensus-building spirit of the Constituent Assembly and urged young citizens to fulfill their responsibilities toward the nation while exercising their guaranteed rights.

articles.headline: President Murmu highlights judicial pendency as challenge to timely justice
articles.summary: President Droupadi Murmu stated that the high number of pending cases in Indian courts is a major challenge for the justice delivery system. Speaking on Constitution Day, she emphasized that timely access is essential to the concept of justice and expressed confidence in ongoing efforts like technology utilization and procedural simplification to resolve the issue.

articles.headline: India records foodgrain production of 378.53 million tonnes in 2025-26
articles.summary: Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced a record foodgrain production of 378.53 million tonnes for 2025-26. This is 20.8 million tonnes higher than the previous year. Rice and wheat production reached 155.15 million and 122.06 million tonnes respectively. India remains the world's largest producer of pulses, jute, millets, and spices.

articles.headline: New U.S. tariffs on India seen as pressure for trade deal
articles.summary: Exporters and trade experts suggest the proposed 25% U.S. tariff on Indian goods is a tactic to push for a trade deal. The USTR proposal includes a reduction to 17% if an agreement is signed. However, analysts believe the tariffs pose a limited threat as over 50% of Indian exports to the U.S., such as drugs and electronics, have sticky pricing.

articles.headline: Global shipping growth stagnates in 2026 amid geopolitical conflicts
articles.summary: UNCTAD reports that global seaborne trade growth fell to 1.9% in 2025 and expects zero growth in 2026. Conflicts in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz have choked major routes. India has emerged as a beneficiary as shipping lines divert vessels to Mundra and Nhava Sheva ports. Container capacity at Mundra increased by 53% between February and June 2026.

articles.headline: C-DAC plans indigenous GPU development by mid-2028
articles.summary: The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) aims to develop a full-fledged indigenous GPU by 2028 to reduce price pressure from global suppliers. The institution is seeking private sector partners for manufacturing and commercialization. The chip architecture will support LLM training and edge analytics, with an intermediate 30-core chip expected by mid-2027.

articles.headline: Israeli air strikes kill nine in Gaza, including Hamas official
articles.summary: Israeli military operations in Gaza killed at least nine Palestinians overnight, including the Hamas-appointed Deputy Minister of Education Khaled Abu Nada and his wife. The strikes occurred amid a third consecutive night of intense air attacks. Hamas described the targeting of academics and civilian figures as a heinous crime.

articles.headline: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing rejects some ICJ genocide requirements
articles.summary: Myanmar's military leader Min Aung Hlaing stated the government will refuse to fully comply with International Court of Justice requirements regarding genocide against the Rohingya minority. While acting on some measures, he rejected others as 'inappropriate'. The ICJ found the country responsible for genocide in its previous rulings.

articles.headline: U.K. net migration falls to lowest level since 1997
articles.summary: Net migration to the United Kingdom fell to 77,000 in the year ending June 2026, the lowest annual figure since 1997. The drop was driven by a significant decrease in non-EU nationals arriving for study and work. Indians remain the largest foreign group immigrating to and emigrating from the U.K., with 44,000 arriving for work and 77,000 for study.

articles.headline: Drone attack in Kuwait kills two Italian technicians
articles.summary: A drone strike on Kuwaiti military installations killed two Italian technicians working on an air-defence system. Italian officials claimed the drones were Iranian-made. Iran has denied involvement and offered a joint investigation. The attack follows rising tensions in the Persian Gulf and contests over the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: Sheikh Hasina’s planned return tests Bangladesh’s political stability
articles.summary: Former PM Sheikh Hasina announced plans to return to Bangladesh from India on December 16, Victory Day. The current BNP government stated she could only return via extradition to face trial for crimes investigated by the International Crimes Tribunal. Hasina’s return gambit has energized Awami League activists while raising fears of renewed civil unrest.

articles.headline: Sri Lanka-A eliminate India-A to reach Asia Cup final
articles.summary: Sri Lanka-A defeated a star-studded India-A by eight wickets in Doha to reach the Asia Cup Rising Stars final. Centuries from Lasith Croospulle (116) and Sineth Jayawardene (105) helped chase down India's 317 for eight with 8.3 overs to spare. Despite half-centuries from Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma, India-A's poor fielding proved costly.

articles.headline: Methodological flaws found in collagen supplement research studies
articles.summary: An investigation published in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology uncovered significant statistical and methodological errors in studies supporting collagen supplements. Biostatisticians found that industry-funded trials often used inaccurate measurements and short follow-up periods. Evidence that oral collagen meaningfully reverses skin ageing remains unconvincing.

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders clearer labels for high sugar salt and fat
articles.summary: The Supreme Court directed FSSAI to ensure front-of-pack labeling clearly identifies high sugar, salt, and fat content in food. The court emphasized that a one-year transition period for industry compliance must not be misused. FSSAI proposed a red hexagonal design representing 'nutrients of concern' to help consumers identify products with excessive unhealthy ingredients.

articles.headline: Top States report mixed capital expenditure spend for April-October period
articles.summary: Capital expenditure by India's top states grew 1.3% year-on-year to ₹1.39-lakh crore during April-October 2026. Performance was uneven, with Karnataka reporting a 50.9% surge while Tamil Nadu and West Bengal saw declines of 11% and 4% respectively. Analysts cite slower public works and state-specific government decisions on borrowing and project stalling as key factors for the mixed results.

articles.headline: Foreign investors shift from global AI stocks to Indian IT
articles.summary: Technology shares led the Indian market on Thursday, with the Nifty IT index gaining 3.66%. FIIs are rotating funds out of global AI-linked stocks into the Indian IT services sector, which has seen nearly 8% growth over the past week. This shift comes despite softness in other sectors like auto, banks, and FMCG, as investors seek value in domestic technology majors.

articles.headline: Adani and Embraer explore larger stake in proposed joint venture
articles.summary: Adani Defence & Aerospace and Brazil's Embraer are discussing a structural change in their proposed civilian aircraft joint venture. Adani aims for a 51% controlling stake, leaving Embraer with 49%, reflecting a model used in the defense sector. The two entities are working to manufacture regional aircraft in India, with plans for an assembly line at the Dholera Special Investment Region.

articles.headline: Flipkart leadership transition begins as Kalyan Krishnamurthy exits
articles.summary: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy is stepping down as the e-commerce giant undergoes a major leadership transition. The company is evaluating whether to double down on new opportunities like food delivery and quick commerce or consolidate existing businesses. This change comes as rivals like Zepto and Blinkit expand, putting pressure on the Walmart-owned firm's unit economics and growth.

articles.headline: TVS pares Swiss e-bike exposure as overseas bets lose ₹1,158 crore
articles.summary: TVS Motor is restructuring its loss-making Swiss e-bike business, seeking to transfer its e-retail operations to a strategic investor. The company's overseas ventures reported combined losses of ₹1,158 crore in FY26. While TVS will retain the product portfolio and brand, the move aims to curb mounting financial bleeding caused by supply chain disruptions and shifting consumer demand.

articles.headline: Neopolis eyes ₹500 crore revenue from bag brand Carpisa
articles.summary: Neopolis Brands aims to grow its Carpisa brand to 25 retail touchpoints by 2027, targeting ₹500 crore in revenue. The company plans to expand its premium handbag and luggage presence across five Indian cities, including Mumbai and Jaipur. Neopolis holds a 20-year license for Carpisa in India and Sri Lanka and is investing in brand-building and expansion into the luxury-mass market segment.

articles.headline: Mafatlal Industries targets $1 billion revenue by end of decade
articles.summary: Mafatlal Industries CEO Priyavrata Mafatlal expects the firm to reach $1 billion in revenue within the next five years. The company is focusing on three main pillars: uniform manufacturing for schools and defense, digital infrastructure for institutions, and technical textiles. The strategy includes a shift toward asset-light models and a significant expansion in the retail garment market.

articles.headline: India remains a high growth market for Japanese retailer Uniqlo
articles.summary: Uniqlo India reported a 44% revenue growth in FY26, reaching ₹1,724 crore. CFO Kenji Inoue stated the brand plans to continue its aggressive expansion by adding 30-40% more stores annually. The retailer is looking to enter tier-II cities like Chandigarh and Jaipur, viewing India as a critical market for global sourcing and production due to its strong domestic growth and large consumer base.

articles.headline: Hindustan Zinc and IIT Madras develop zinc-air battery prototype
articles.summary: Hindustan Zinc and IIT Madras have developed an electric three-wheeler prototype powered by a zinc-air battery. The 1 kWh battery is designed to supplement lithium-ion packs and potentially extend driving range. This technology is seen as a cost-effective alternative for green mobility, using domestic zinc resources to reduce dependence on imported battery materials like lithium.

articles.headline: India prepares rebuttal to US excess capacity charges in January
articles.summary: The Commerce Department is preparing a rebuttal against US allegations that India's industrial policies have led to excess manufacturing capacity. A public hearing is scheduled for January 2027 by the USTR. India argues that its production-linked incentive (PLI) schemes are aimed at self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) rather than creating structural excess capacity to distort global trade.

articles.headline: Fresh US Section 301 tariff proposal clouds Indian export outlook
articles.summary: A US proposal for new Section 301 tariffs of up to 25% has created uncertainty for Indian exporters, particularly in chemicals, steel, and electronics. Trade bodies warn that these levies would add to existing tariff regimes and burden Indian manufacturers with higher costs. Experts suggest the move reflects a fundamental lack of trust from the US regarding global trade structural issues.

articles.headline: India requires $500 billion annually to reach net zero by 2070
articles.summary: A report by BCG and the Wealth and Alternate Capital Association suggests India needs cumulative investment of $22-24 trillion to meet its 2070 net-zero goal. This equates to nearly $500 billion every year. While climate financing reached $31 billion between 2021 and 2026, the report highlights a massive gap that requires mobilized capital and new approaches for diverse technology stages.

articles.headline: Power sector share in coal offtake hits 13-month high in October
articles.summary: The share of the power sector in total coal offtake rose to 81% in October 2026, the highest in 13 months. This surge followed a 14% rise in thermal power generation due to erratic monsoon patterns and increased industrial demand. Coal India Limited supplied 64.84 million tonnes of coal to thermal power plants during the month to ensure steady electricity supply and prevent fuel shortages.

articles.headline: RBI receives ₹11,189 crore in bids for State Development Loans auction
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India received bids worth ₹11,189.055 crore for its first-ever conversion auction of State Development Loans (SDLs). Against a notified amount of ₹10,800 crore from five states—Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh—the RBI accepted ₹8,002.80 crore. The auction allows states to switch shorter-tenure securities for longer-maturity ones.

articles.headline: Infrastructure projects cost overrun hits ₹3.28 lakh crore in October
articles.summary: A government report reveals that 1,862 central infrastructure projects worth over ₹150 crore each had a total cost overrun of ₹3.28 lakh crore by October 2026. The initial anticipated cost of ₹34.82 lakh crore rose to ₹38.11 lakh crore. Delays were noted in 840 projects, with the report highlighting significant financial slippage across various ministries and development sectors.

articles.headline: CII wins global leadership award for MSME development
articles.summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) has been awarded for outstanding leadership in MSME development at the 2026 International Trade Council GoGlobal Awards in London. The award recognizes CII's contribution to facilitating international market access for Indian MSMEs and strengthening the export ecosystem through its Market Facilitation Services and various development initiatives.

articles.headline: Nvidia board faces questions over compliance and US export rules
articles.summary: Nvidia’s board is under scrutiny following reports that CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a former Megaspeed executive may have masked violations of US export controls. Concerns involve potential diversion of restricted AI chips to China through intermediaries. Investors and regulators are questioning the board’s oversight and Nvidia’s liability regarding financial market disclosures.

articles.headline: Consolidation of Regional Rural Banks ignores needs of large States
articles.summary: The 'One State One RRB' policy is facing criticism for ignoring the diverse developmental needs of large states like Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. While intended for administrative efficiency, analysts argue that massive consolidation has reduced the number of RRBs from 196 to 28, harming localized credit knowledge. Critics advocate for multiple RRBs in large states to foster competition and reach.

articles.headline: Trump aims for leverage over China with 40 percent tariff threat
articles.summary: Donald Trump has threatened a 40% effective tariff rate on Chinese goods if Beijing does not comply with critical minerals and agricultural purchase agreements. The move follows a USTR investigation into China's industrial practices. While the proposal aims to secure US interests, experts warn it could complicate global trade and lead to retaliatory measures from China in the tech sector.

articles.headline: Quantum-proofing the Rupee: RBI sets up eight-member expert committee
articles.summary: The RBI has established a panel, Q-SAFE, to develop a roadmap for transitioning India's financial sector to quantum-secure systems. The committee has six months to map inventory and recommend protections against 'harvest now, decrypt later' threats. This move aligns with global security concerns that future quantum computers could compromise current cryptographic standards used in banking.

articles.headline: IT stocks surge helps Nifty and Sensex sustain weekly gains
articles.summary: Indian benchmark indices rose on Thursday, led by a 3.66% jump in the Nifty IT index as foreign investors rotated funds into the sector. The Nifty 50 closed at 25,884.50, up 65.25 points, while the Sensex ended 390 points higher. Gains in TCS, Infosys, and HCL Tech offset declines in auto and banking stocks. Overall market sentiment remains cautious ahead of the upcoming RBI policy meeting.

articles.headline: NSE receives RBI approval for corporate bond index futures
articles.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India has received a No Objection Certificate from the RBI to introduce futures contracts on corporate bond indices. The move is expected to provide market participants with an exchange-traded instrument to manage risk and support the development of the domestic bond market. The initiative aims to enhance transparency and liquidity in the corporate bond segment.

articles.headline: Kotak Neo invests ₹1,000 crore in digital transformation and start-ups
articles.summary: Kotak Securities has committed over ₹1,000 crore to technology and digital infrastructure through its Kotak Neo platform. The firm is acquiring and integrating tech-driven start-ups like TradeGyani and Kotak Connect to enhance its digital-first investing experience. The strategy aims to build a robust ecosystem for tech-savvy investors using advanced analytics and AI-driven platforms.

articles.headline: Schaeffler’s promoter cuts 6.5 percent stake in Indian unit
articles.summary: German industrial supplier Schaeffler has sold a 6.5% stake in its Indian subsidiary via an open market transaction for approximately $330 million. The move is part of the parent company's strategy to increase financial flexibility as it integrates Vitesco Technologies. Schaeffler plans to use the proceeds to support its global transformation toward electric mobility and industrial automation.

articles.headline: BSE Index Services gets SEBI registration as index provider
articles.summary: BSE Index Services Limited has received its certificate of registration from SEBI to operate as an index provider. This allows the BSE subsidiary to strengthen its index-related operations and governance framework. The registration is an important step in providing reliable and credible indices for India's financial markets, covering various asset classes and investment strategies.

articles.headline: Gold loan growth slows as metal price drops trigger collections
articles.summary: Gold loan companies are shifting focus from growth to collections after a sharp fall in metal prices pushed loan-to-value (LTV) ratios higher. Many lenders are asking borrowers to provide additional collateral or pledge more gold as LTVs breached the 75% regulatory limit. Analysts expect asset-quality stress in the segment to rise as lenders grapple with increased risk levels and defaults.

articles.headline: West Asia conflict hits India harder than Russia-Ukraine war
articles.summary: An RBI study suggests the West Asia conflict has had a more significant impact on India's economy than the Russia-Ukraine war. The report highlights that retail petrol and diesel prices rose by 7.4% at the onset of the current conflict, compared to a partial pass-through earlier. Increased global oil prices and currency depreciation remain key concerns for India's trade balance and inflation.

articles.headline: India Inc revenue likely to grow 18-20 percent in Q3
articles.summary: Rating agency ICRA expects corporate India’s revenue to grow by 18-20% year-on-year in the October-December 2026 quarter. However, operating profit margins are likely to shrink by 50-75 basis points due to inflationary pressures and rising input costs. Sectors like automobiles and FMCG are expected to benefit from resilient demand, while energy-intensive industries face margin compression.

articles.headline: Majority of Indian companies expect labor codes to increase costs
articles.summary: A survey by Grant Thornton Bharat shows that 74% of companies expect the new labor codes to increase employee costs. Nearly 50% of firms anticipate an increase in overall costs due to revised definitions of wages and higher contributions to provident funds. Companies identified implementation, payroll management, and compliance changes as the biggest hurdles to transitioning to the new regime.

articles.headline: JNPA awards ₹77-crore shore power contract for Gateway Terminals India
articles.summary: Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority has awarded a ₹77-crore contract to Leena Powertech Engineers for setting up shore power infrastructure at GTI. The project will allow ships to switch off diesel generators and use cleaner grid electricity while at port. This initiative aims to reduce maritime emissions and promote sustainable shipping practices at one of India's largest container ports.

articles.headline: Nirmala Sitharaman holds first pre-Budget meeting with Gen Z representatives
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman conducted a pre-Budget consultation specifically for 'Gen Z' representatives. The meeting focused on jobs, skill development, and investments in AI and emerging technologies. Participants emphasized the need for better industry-academic linkages and career opportunities for young people. This initiative is part of wider consultations for the 2027-28 Budget.

articles.headline: EU rejects entry of two Alang shipyards into approved recycling list
articles.summary: The European Parliament has voted against adding two Indian shipyards at Alang to the EU’s list of approved ship recycling facilities. The rejection, based on concerns over labor safety and environmental standards, means EU-flagged vessels cannot be dismantled at these sites. Environmental groups welcomed the decision, while Indian recyclers expressed disappointment over the move.

articles.headline: India’s semiconductor market set to reach $110 billion by 2030
articles.summary: CareEdge reports that India's semiconductor market is projected to reach $100-110 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 17.8%. The market is currently driven by demand from consumer electronics, mobile communications, and computing. Government incentives through PLI schemes and investments in fab and OSAT facilities are expected to significantly boost domestic manufacturing and supply capacity.

articles.headline: EPAM opens new Chennai office as India headcount tops 14,000
articles.summary: US-based digital transformation firm EPAM Systems has opened a new office in Chennai, its fastest-growing location in India. The company's total India headcount has reached 14,000, growing by 30-40% annually. The expansion follows strong demand for AI-led engineering and managed services. EPAM also operates centers in Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Pune, and Gurugram to serve its global clients.

articles.headline: Special Parliament session starting Monday sparks delimitation buzz
articles.summary: A special Parliament session beginning Monday has led to speculation about legislative action on delimitation and the implementation of the women’s reservation law. The government has moved to reconvene both houses for 'essential government business.' A delimitation exercise based on the upcoming 2027 Census could lead to a significant increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats.

articles.headline: Turkiye tells UN that Cyprus arms activity threatens regional stability
articles.summary: Turkiye has raised concerns at the UN regarding arms buildup in Cyprus, citing India's deal to supply BrahMos supersonic missiles to the Republic of Cyprus. Turkiye claims the military cooperation and potential missile deployment threaten the security balance in the Eastern Mediterranean. India has been expanding its strategic partnerships and defense exports in the region.

articles.headline: Nitin Gadkari unveils ₹1 lakh crore road projects in West Bengal
articles.summary: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari announced new road infrastructure projects worth ₹1 lakh crore for West Bengal. Major projects include a 250-km ring road around Kolkata costing ₹14,000 crore and several high-speed corridors. Gadkari emphasized that the 'double-engine' government in the state would expedite project delivery and support West Bengal's overall growth and industrial development.

articles.headline: Meta battles Congress protest over content removal in India
articles.summary: The Congress party has protested to Meta over the alleged 'automated content-removal' of its social media posts. The party claims that its posts, including birthday greetings and political statements, are being blocked or removed without proper explanation. Meta stated that it moderates content in accordance with Indian IT laws and its global community standards.

articles.headline: Sowing of rabi crops trails by 10 percent due to poor moisture
articles.summary: Rabi crop sowing has fallen by 10% compared to last year, with total acreage at 260.97 lakh hectares as of November 20. Deficient monsoon rainfall in states like Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan has reduced soil moisture for wheat and gram. Wheat acreage is down 22% in M.P. and 28% in Haryana, raising concerns about overall foodgrain production for the upcoming season.

articles.headline: India’s steel output up 3.6 percent in October
articles.summary: India's crude steel production grew by 3.6% year-on-year to 14.5 million tonnes in October 2026. Global steel output, however, saw a slight decline of 1.1%. India maintained its position as the world's second-largest steel producer. Production growth was supported by domestic demand, while global output was dragged down by lower production in China and other major producing nations.

articles.headline: Common medicines fail quality tests in latest CDSCO report
articles.summary: Several widely used medicines, including Telmisartan (BP), Paracetamol (pain), and Folic Acid, failed quality tests conducted by the CDSCO in October 2026. Out of 2,213 samples analyzed, 83 batches of Telmisartan 40 mg failed for dissolution and assay. The drug regulator has declared these batches as 'not of standard quality,' raising concerns about pharmaceutical manufacturing standards.

articles.headline: US flags India’s 87 percent antibiotic reliance on China
articles.summary: A USTR report highlights that India remains heavily dependent on China for active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), importing 87% of its requirements from there. Despite India's strong presence in the global generics market, this reliance is seen as a strategic vulnerability. The report notes that US-funded projects are working to diversify and enhance India's domestic API production.

articles.headline: Hetero begins shipping generic lenacapavir for HIV prevention in Africa
articles.summary: Hetero has started shipping the first generic version of lenacapavir to Africa, with an initial supply of 300,000 vials to South Africa, Uganda, and Zimbabwe. Lenacapavir is an injectable HIV prevention drug administered twice a year. The generic version is being produced under a voluntary licensing agreement with Gilead Sciences to improve access to life-saving medication in the region.

articles.headline: Tech Mahindra plans to revive satcom business with Comviva
articles.summary: Tech Mahindra is looking to revitalize its satellite communication business through its subsidiary Comviva. The company sees significant opportunities in blending terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks as satellite-to-mobile services gain traction. Tech Mahindra expects the satcom sector to be a key growth driver, with its subsidiary already seeing demand for digital and IoT services.

articles.headline: NITES union calls for AI-driven job protection framework
articles.summary: The Nascent Information Technology Employees Senate (NITES) has written to the Labor Ministry seeking a framework to protect IT employees from AI-driven job losses. The union argues that AI is directly replacing jobs and that existing labor laws do not provide adequate protection. NITES is calling for policy discussions and mandatory training programs for affected workers.

articles.headline: Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams receives record ₹206 crore gold donation
articles.summary: A record donation of 47 gold ornaments worth approximately ₹206 crore was made to the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) by an anonymous donor. The donation, handed over to Andhra Pradesh CM N Chandrababu Naidu, is one of the largest in TTD's history. TTD authorities have confirmed the record-breaking nature of the gift, which further adds to the temple's substantial gold reserves.

articles.headline: Bengaluru court allows Darshan’s petition for back pain treatment
articles.summary: A city court has directed prison authorities to facilitate actor Darshan’s treatment for back pain at Victoria Hospital. Darshan, who has been receiving physiotherapy at the prison hospital, approached the court stating that previous treatments were not yielding results. The court also noted a separate petition seeking permission for treatment at a private hospital.

articles.headline: Elon Musk plans to gift SpaceX shares to every child in US
articles.summary: Elon Musk has announced plans to gift every child in the United States two SpaceX shares to build public support for his satellite and AI businesses. Children would receive one share from the company and one from Musk personally once his lockup period expires in June next year. The giveaway is estimated to be worth approximately $18 billion.

articles.headline: Bescom to refund consumers 35 paise per unit from April
articles.summary: Power consumers under Bescom in Karnataka are set to receive a refund of up to 35 paise per unit for 12 months starting April 2027. The utility reported a profit of Rs 293.6 crore in 2025-26 due to improved billing efficiency and revenue recovery. This marks the first time in years that power utilities have decided to pass profits to consumers.

articles.headline: IBM ends work visa and green card sponsorship in consulting arm
articles.summary: IBM has decided to discontinue H-1B work visa and green card sponsorship for most roles within its consulting division, affecting thousands of professionals. Affected employees have been given three weeks to decide on relocation outside the US or leave the company by the end of 2026. IBM cited evolving business demands and the availability of skilled workers for the policy change.

articles.headline: Grand Bihar wedding of MLA's daughter makes global headlines
articles.summary: The five-day wedding of Mokama MLA Anant Singh’s daughter in Patna district has gained international attention for its massive scale and display of wealth. Dubbed a 'royal wedding,' the event featured six helipads and catered to roughly 400,000 guests. The extravagance has drawn criticism and irony given Bihar's status as India's poorest state.

articles.headline: SC slams MNCs for producing inferior products for Indian consumers
articles.summary: The Supreme Court called out the 'double standard' of multinational companies producing lower-quality food for India compared to Western nations. The court urged food business operators to adopt uniform global standards for additives and composition. It asserted that Indian consumers are entitled to the same health protection as those in the US or UK.

articles.headline: Gujarat High Court summons police brass over missing ex-judge
articles.summary: The Gujarat High Court has summoned the state's highest police authority after a retired judge remained missing for three years without an FIR being registered. Rajeshkumar Oza went missing in 2023, and his daughter filed a habeas corpus petition alleging police apathy.
